title: Venus Has No Moon: The Slow Spin That May Have Swallowed One
title_zh: 金星没有卫星：缓慢的自转或许让它吞下了自己的月亮
intro_zh: 本文约 525 词，围绕一项新研究展开：金星极慢的自转可能让原本属于它的卫星螺旋式向内坠落，最终撞上行星本身。文章按科普说明的顺序展开，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: Venus is easy to find. On many evenings it shines brightly in the western sky, and it is the planet next door to Earth. People sometimes call it our twin, because the two worlds are alike in size. Yet it has no moon at all. New research suggests that this empty sky is not simply a matter of luck. Venus may once have had a moon, and later destroyed it.
paragraphs.zh: 金星很容易被找到。在许多傍晚，它明亮地闪耀在西方天空，是地球的邻星。人们有时称它为我们的“孪生兄弟”，因为这两个世界大小相近。然而它根本没有卫星。一项新研究显示，这片空荡的天空并非只是运气问题。金星也许曾经拥有过一颗卫星，后来把它毁掉了。

paragraphs.en: Earth's moon behaves very differently. Over a very long period, it gradually moves a little farther away from us every year. The change is far too slow for anyone to notice in a lifetime, but the direction is always outward. Computer models show that a moon around Venus would have taken the opposite path. Instead of drifting away, it would have moved closer and closer, step by step, until there was no space left between them.
paragraphs.zh: 地球的月亮表现完全不同。在极其漫长的时间里，它每年都逐渐离我们远一点点。这种变化慢得人在一生中都察觉不到，但方向始终朝外。计算机模型显示，围绕金星的卫星会走上相反的道路：它不是逐渐漂离，而是一步步越来越近，直到彼此之间再无空隙。

paragraphs.en: The reason lies in rotation. Venus turns on its axis extremely slowly, much more slowly than Earth. A planet's spin decides how its gravity pulls on a moon. When the spin is fast, as it is on Earth, the moon is pushed gently outwards. When the spin is slow, that push weakens and then reverses, so the moon begins to lose energy rather than gain it. Energy lost means height lost, and the path around the planet grows smaller.
paragraphs.zh: 原因在于自转。金星绕轴自转极其缓慢，比地球慢得多。行星的自转速度决定了它的引力如何拉扯卫星。自转快时（如地球），卫星被轻轻往外推；自转慢时，这种推力会减弱甚至反向，于是卫星开始损失能量而非获得能量。失去能量就意味着降低高度，环绕行星的路径也就越来越小。

paragraphs.en: Researchers built computer simulations of a young Venus with a moon circling it. In the models, the moon refused to stay put. It began to spiral inward, losing height with every circle it completed. In the end, the path finished with a crash: the moon struck the planet that it had once traveled around.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员构建了年轻金星带着一颗卫星绕转的计算机模拟。在模型中，这颗卫星没有安分地待着，而是开始向内螺旋式下降，每绕完一圈就降低一些高度。最终，这条路径以一次撞击结束：卫星撞上了它曾经环绕的行星。

paragraphs.en: The models also produced a result that may surprise people. Size mattered, but not in the way one might expect. A larger moon fell faster. A bigger body feels a stronger pull, and so its inward movement speeds up. Smaller moons lasted longer, yet they too were unlikely to avoid the same violent end. The difference was not small, and it appeared again and again whenever the starting conditions were changed.
paragraphs.zh: 模型还得出了一个可能令人意外的结果。大小确实重要，但方式与人们的预想不同：较大的卫星下落得更快。天体越大，受到的拉扯越强，向内的运动也就越快。较小的卫星撑得更久，但它们同样难以避免同样的剧烈结局。这种差别并不小，而且每当改变初始条件时，它都会反复出现。

paragraphs.en: Today Venus is a world of thick clouds and extreme heat, and its sky holds no moon. The slow turning of the planet may be part of the reason why. If the idea is correct, the moon did not simply leave. It came down. Venus, in a sense, swallowed its own moon, and no large piece of it stayed in the sky afterwards.
paragraphs.zh: 如今的金星是一个被厚厚云层和极端高温包裹的世界，它的天空中没有任何卫星。行星缓慢的自转也许正是原因之一。如果这一想法正确，那颗卫星并不是简单地离去了——它是掉了下来。某种意义上，金星吞掉了自己的卫星，此后天上再没有留下它的大块残骸。

paragraphs.en: This idea is a model, not a proven fact. Nobody can send a machine to watch something that may have happened billions of years ago. What the study offers is a careful description of how a moon could lose its orbit and disappear, one that fits the way Venus turns today. It gives scientists a clear question to test.
paragraphs.zh: 这个想法是一种模型，而不是已被证实的事实。没有人能派一台机器去观察数十亿年前可能发生的事。这项研究提供的，是对一颗卫星如何失去轨道并消失的细致描述，而且与金星今天的自转方式相符。它给科学家留下了一个清晰的、可供检验的问题。

paragraphs.en: Why should anyone care? Venus and Earth are neighbors of similar size, yet one is full of life and the other is not. Comparing them helps us understand which conditions matter. A missing moon is one more small piece in a much larger puzzle about our own planet and its long, quiet history.
paragraphs.zh: 为什么这值得关心？金星和地球是大小相近的邻居，但一个充满生命，另一个却没有。比较它们有助于我们理解哪些条件至关重要。少了一颗卫星，只是关于我们自身行星及其漫长而安静历史这幅更大拼图中的又一小块。

questions.q: What does the new research suggest about a moon that once circled Venus?
options: It would have drifted slowly away from Venus.
It would have moved closer to Venus and finally hit it.
It would have broken into many small pieces.
It would have stopped moving and stayed in place.
questions.explain: 文章第二、四段指出，围绕金星的卫星不会像地球的月亮那样逐渐远离，而是不断向内接近，最终撞上行星。A 项与原文相反；C、D 两项文中并未提及。

questions.q: According to the passage, how did larger moons behave in the computer models?
options: They fell faster than smaller moons.
questions.explain: 第五段明确说明：较大的卫星下落得更快，因为天体越大受到的拉扯越强，向内运动也越快。B、C、D 均与原文不符。

questions.q: Why is Venus's slow spin important in the explanation?
options: It makes the planet much hotter than Earth.
It prevents any moon from forming near the planet.
It weakens and then reverses the outward push on a moon.
It makes the planet's gravity disappear over time.
questions.explain: 第三段指出，自转快时卫星被轻轻往外推；自转慢时这种推力减弱并反向，卫星因此损失能量而降低高度。A 虽属常识，但文中并未用它来解释卫星消失；B、D 属错误推断。

questions.q: What does the phrase 'spiral inward' most probably mean in the passage?
options: to move in a curved path that gets closer and closer
questions.explain: 'spiral inward' 指螺旋式向内运动，即沿弯曲路径一圈圈靠近行星，与第四段“每绕完一圈就降低一些高度”的描述一致。

source.name: ScienceDaily
source.title: Venus may have swallowed its own moon
